Specifies whether speech recognition operates in continuous recognition mode, i.e. the recognizer will continuously listen and recognize speech until stopped. Defaults to .

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with the specified recognized text.
member.param: The current full text recognized from the speech input.
A number between 0 and 1 representing the confidence of the speech-to-text transcription. In case a confidence score cannot be provided, leave this value to be -1.

The Elastic batch API looks like: curl -X POST \"https://bi-progress.es.eastus2.azure.elastic-cloud.com:443/_bulk?pretty\" \\ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\ -H \"Authorization: ApiKey $API_KEY\" \\ -d' \\ { \"index\": { \"_index\": \"logs-bi-devtools-xxx\" } } { \"message\": \"{ \\\"Type\\\":\\\"LicenseUsed\\\",\\\"UserId\\\":\\\"2aaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee\\\" }\" } With a trailing new-line! The objects described here are send as a \"message\" one on a line. Looks like application/x-ndjson

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

source.

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .
The Telerik product name. .
productCode.
componentSuite.
referenceType.

Target framework as read from the csproj file. It will be in the format [TargetFrameworkIdentifier(TFI)],Version=v[TargetFrameworkVersion(TFV)] e.g. .NETCoreApp,Version=v5.0. More info about these [here](https://github.com/dotnet/designs/blob/main/accepted/2020/net5/net5.md#mapping-to-properties). .
isTrial.

member.name: T:Telerik.CallHome.OpenAPI.Model.BuildType
member.summary: Build type indicates if the tests run on PR, Nightly builds, manually on a local developer machines. Nightly - are builds that run regularly, runs all tests, against the main branch. PullRequest - are builds running after a developer opens a PR, and performs tests as part of continuous integration, these tests can sometime fail due developer introduced errors. ManuallyTriggered - are builds triggered by a developer, wheter it is locally on the developer's machine or manually triggered automated builds like release related tests.

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .

productCode.

referenceType.
Determines the license type of the product. Dev = 0, Trial = 1 Free = 2 .
A product version, possibly sem-ver, but also some product use date string based versioning system. .

Target framework as read from the csproj file. It will be in the format [TargetFrameworkIdentifier(TFI)],Version=v[TargetFrameworkVersion(TFV)] e.g. .NETCoreApp,Version=v5.0. More info about these [here](https://github.com/dotnet/designs/blob/main/accepted/2020/net5/net5.md#mapping-to-properties). .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .

member.name: T:Telerik.CallHome.OpenAPI.Model.ExtensionInstallBase
member.summary: An event tracking which extensions are installed on actively used machine. This event happens when an IDE, that has the extension installed, is opened. The event fires event without the user actively using an extension feature. Occurances may be aggregated and the event could fire once a day or once a week. Don't use in \"count\" queries. Use the 'ExtensionInstallBase' event in \"distinct_count(machine-id) per month\" to track: - The size of an extension install base - The extension retention rates - The extension churn rates

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .

member.name: T:Telerik.CallHome.OpenAPI.Model.LicenseInformation
member.summary: An event tracking the telerik license for a telerik product. The VS and VS Code IDEs will perform a look up for a kendo-ui-license.txt or SetScriptKey in the client's code, and try to provide information about the license associated to ProductUsed and ComponentUsed. This event has similar debounce mechanisms to that of ProductUsed and ComponentUsed and will be fired once per day or once per session.

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .

The 'LicenseNotValid' constant..

The error code for the detected license error. For example: * TKL101 - Product not licensed * TKL102 - Expired perpetual license * TKL103 - Expired subscription license * TKL104 - Grace subscription license (up to 10 days after expiry) * TKL105 - Expired trial license .
For backward compatibility this is string, but as of today we support one of: * trial * perpetual * subscription .
The expiration date of the product license (ISO without milliseconds, e.g. 2025-02-21T08:42:51Z)..
A Telerik signed JWT containing UserID. Used as evidence that the events originated from a client..
UserID can be used to associate telemetry data with personal account details. User consent have to be provided before the data is associated with the account details. .
LicenseID can be used to associate licensing events with an instance of telerik-license.txt generated on telerik.com .
productCode.
A product version, possibly sem-ver, but also some product use date string based versioning system. .
Indicates if the license is used in a CI environment of the specified type. A `null` value indicates that the license is not used in a CI environment..

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .

Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: Indicates if the license is used in a CI environment of the specified type. A `null` value indicates that the license is not used in a CI environment..

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.

member.name: T:Telerik.CallHome.OpenAPI.Model.NotificationType
member.summary: The type of the displayed notification. Notifications could be shown in different combinations. - NewerVersion - shown when the version referenced in the loaded project/solution is older than the one available for download - NewerLocalVersion - shown when the version referenced in the loaded project/solution is older than the one available locally - Trial - shown when trial version is referenced in the loaded project/solution - SubscriptionExpiring - shown when user has a subscription that is about to expire starts showing 60 days before and stops 60 days after license expiration. - SubscriptionExpired - shown when user has a subscription that is expired - TrialToDev - shown when a trial version is referenced in the loaded project/solution and a dev version is available locally - Telemetry - shown when consent to collect product usage information and associate it with the account details is given

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .
The Telerik product name. .

There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .
productCode.

member.name: T:Telerik.CallHome.OpenAPI.Model.ProductCode
member.summary: A Telerik product code. Usually one of the Telerik UI for * or Kendo UI for *. Some of the products have subvariants and are additionally identified by the ComponentSuite. For example UI for jQuery can be initialized with MVVM, Angular or jQuery Plugins. Table of ProductCode (+ ComponentSuites where applicable): - RCAJAX: \"Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX\" - KENDOUIMVC: \"Telerik UI for ASP.NET MVC\" - MVC - UIASPCORE: \"Telerik UI for ASP.NET Core\" - CORE - CORETagHelpers - BLAZOR: \"Telerik UI for Blazor\" - Blazor - KENDOUICOMPLETE: \"Kendo UI for jQuery\" - MVVM - Angular - Web - KENDOUIREACT: \"KendoReact\" - React - ReactWrappers (Legacy React UI suite using react wrappers, superseded by native React components) - KENDOUIVUE: \"Kendo UI for Vue\" - Vue - KENDOUIANGULAR: \"Kendo UI for Angular\" - Angular2 - RCWPF: (RadControls) \"Telerik UI for WPF\" - RCWPF - RCWPFXAML (The Xaml variant of RCWPF assemblies) - RCWPFNOXAML (The NoXaml variant of RCWPF assemblies) - RCWF: (RadControls) \"Telerik UI for WinForms\" - WINUI: \"Telerik UI for WinUI\" - UIXAM: \"Telerik UI for Xamarin\" - MAUI: \"Telerik UI for MAUI\" - REPORTING: \"Telerik Reporting\" - DPL: (Document Processing Library) \"DPL\" - 811: \"Telerik JustMock Lite\" - JM: \"Telerik JustMock\" - REPORTSERVER: \"Telerik Report Server\" - DPLDEMOS: \"Telerik Document Processing Demos\"

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .
oSPlatform.
Operating system version in form \"<major>.<minor>\", patch and build are ignored. See dotnet: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.osversion?view=netframework-4.7.2 .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .
Checks if the user has JetBrains Rider naively by looking if any of the directories exist: - C:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - D:/Program Files/JetBrains/Rider/ - /Applications/Rider.app/ .
A non-null string identifying usage on CI environment. Having this set to non null or empty string indicates the Telerik product was probably used by non-dev automation. .

A timestamp. Formatted in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.ffffZ. See also ISO 8601. Example: In the macos installer scripts we used `date -u +%FT%T.%3Z` Example: In the Splunk we have: \"2022-01-30T11:49:00.3Z\", \"2022-01-30T11:49:03.4675419Z\"; Example: In a C# client we use `DateTime.UtcNow.ToString(\"o\")` .

A string identifying a test suite. Some repositories may contain multiple Unit and E2E suites, that generate multiple reports. Each such test run is expected to be reported under a different suite name. E.g. the vscode-extensions repo may perform a single unit tests job, that would report metrics for: \"VSCode jQuery snippet unit tests\" and \"VSCode Angular snippet unit tests\" This field should not identify a particular run within a test matrix. For example, if a repo has unit tests for a package, and it runs on node 14, node 16 and node 18, on MacOS, Windows and Linux, all 9 test runs of the same suite should report under the same TestSuite. To identify these 9 test runs see TestMatrix. .

Identifies a test matrix instance. This string should identify the test environment in which the TestSuite was executed. For example if a repo has a suite TestSuite = \"Grid unit tests\", and these run under node 14, node 16, node 18, MacOS, Windows and Linux, suitable TestMatrix values for each test run would be: - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 14, MacOS\" - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 16, MacOS\" - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 18, MacOS\" - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 14, Windows\" - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 16, Windows\" - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 18, Windows\" - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 14, Linux\" - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 16, Linux\" - TestSuite=\"Grid unit tests\", TestMatrix=\"node 18, Linux\" .
A relative file path to the test result file used to generate the test run metric. .

member.name: P:Telerik.CallHome.OpenAPI.Model.TestRun.TestSuite
member.summary: A string identifying a test suite. Some repositories may contain multiple Unit and E2E suites, that generate multiple reports. Each such test run is expected to be reported under a different suite name. E.g. the vscode-extensions repo may perform a single unit tests job, that would report metrics for: \"VSCode jQuery snippet unit tests\" and \"VSCode Angular snippet unit tests\" This field should not identify a particular run within a test matrix. For example, if a repo has unit tests for a package, and it runs on node 14, node 16 and node 18, on MacOS, Windows and Linux, all 9 test runs of the same suite should report under the same TestSuite. To identify these 9 test runs see TestMatrix.

member.name: T:Telerik.CallHome.OpenAPI.Model.TestType
member.summary: Please stick to Unit or E2E. Example of E2E would be WebDriver based tests that launch websites using a web app built using Kendo UI and testing the Kendo UI controls in the app. Developers should be able to run them, but these are usually maintained by QA. Slow. Example of Component tests would be to use DOM simulation and test Kendo UI tree in node, without WebDriver or similar. For mobile, it would mean running a mobile app with unit tests, that does not involve AppDriver to run the tests. Still fast execution and developer are expected to run them before PR. Example of Unit tests would be dotnet test performing isolated test on small amount of classes, executed by the developers, extremely quick execution. Used for the benefits of TDD.

Slow. Example of Component tests would be to use DOM simulation and test Kendo UI tree in node, without WebDriver or similar. For mobile, it would mean running a mobile app with unit tests, that does not involve AppDriver to run the tests. Still fast execution and developer are expected to run them before PR. Example of Unit tests would be dotnet test performing isolated test on small amount of classes, executed by the developers, extremely quick execution. Used for the benefits of TDD.

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Random GUID identifying single usage session in the context of our tracking. Try to create a GUID once in the lifetime of an application. Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. Example: DCEAAD12-E11B-47FA-BBF8-19E7ADB5CCD5 Example: In C# `Guid.NewGuid().ToString().ToUpperInvariant()` would generate a guid. .

This will either be unset, or set to true for internal Progress machines. Setting the environment variable \"TELERIK_TELEMETRY_INTERNAL\" to \"TRUE\", should toggle the CallHome client to send `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. Telerik developers and CI machines should set this environment variable, so they don't offset the usage for new features. Usage sensitive dashboards should filter events containing `{ IsInternalUsage: true }`. .

Encoded ID generated on base of BIOS, HDD and CPU ids. There is a whole separate Telerik library accessing a lot of OS APIs to collect the hardware information, and then pass it through a hashing function so the id can be hardware related but not reversible (e.g. id -> PC conversion is impossible) .

Consider passing the session through environment variables or command line parameters to internal processes. member.name: T:Telerik.CallHome.Debouncing.SynchronizedIsolatedStorageDebouncer`2
member.summary:
This instance of a uses an OS wide named Mutex for access synchronization to a time table database. The time table is stored on an isolated storage and file access locks the file explicitly. Throws if the file access fails or if the lock can not be acquired in certain time.
Note the global named Mutex is shared for all users, while the file access is user owned. This means that multiple users running on the same machine may wait each other for access, but they will use separate time table files.

A serializable lookup key generated for the filtered instances.

member.summary:
Set the "TELERIK_TELEMETRY_DEBOUNCE" environment variable to - "OFF" - "CLEAR" to manage the debouncers
OFF: Will switch off debouncers and will send all events. (will not limit certain events to be sent once per 24 hours) CLEAR: Will clear the debounce tables for events that are sent once per 24 hours
Otherwise the call home client will keep its default behaviour.

member.name: F:Telerik.Licensing.Status.Obtrusiveness.DismissibleNotice
member.summary:
Show as a small notification message at the corner of the app. The message can be closed. No watermarks would appear.
Should barely affect testing.
The message must indicate that this is a non-product version of the Telerik product.
Fallbacks: In case these toast notifications can't be implemented you can use a behavior similar to DimissibleOverlay, but the watermarks should not be displayed, or if displayed the watermarks must be removed when the dialog is closed. User interaction must not be blocked
For documents - print in header or footer or as a strike through the message, because this is a non-production version of the Telerik product.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.Animation.RadAnimation
member.summary: Represents an abstract base class for creating animations in a user interface. The RadAnimation class provides properties to define the name, repeat behavior, and speed ratio of an animation, along with methods to create and update animations for UI controls. Derived classes should implement the CreateAnimation method to generate specific animations, while the UpdateAnimation method can be overridden to adjust the timing and behavior of the storyboard before playback. This class serves as the foundation for animation management in UI applications, allowing for flexible and reusable animation logic.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.Primitives.RadUniformGrid
member.summary: Represents a uniform grid panel that arranges its child elements in a structured grid format, distributing space evenly among them. The grid can be configured to hide the first row or column, preserve space for collapsed children, and allows for orientation settings to control the flow of child elements (horizontal or vertical). The adapts its layout based on the number of defined rows and columns, measuring and arranging child elements accordingly. By default, the grid's orientation is horizontal, and its initial columns and rows are set to zero.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadBusyIndicator
member.summary: Represents a control that indicates a busy state of an application or a specific process. The allows customization of the busy indication through various properties such as , , and . It can be used to inform users that an operation is in progress, thereby improving user experience. Additionally, the control supports customization of the overlay and progress bar styles through the and properties. It includes functionality for displaying a localized message during the busy state via the property, which can bind a localized string to the indicator. The property specifies the duration after which the busy indicator is shown, allowing it to avoid flickering for very brief operations. The control also supports indeterminate progress indication through the property. Use this control in situations where feedback is needed while an application is busy performing tasks, such as loading data or processing user input.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadButton
member.summary: Represents a customizable button control within the Telerik UI for WPF framework. The RadButton class derives from the Button class and includes additional properties, events, and behaviors that enhance its functionality, such as support for hover effects, corner radius customization, and command binding. It introduces dependency properties like HoverDelay to manage hover interactions, CornerRadius and InnerCornerRadius for visual styling, and routed events like Activate and Hover to handle button interactions. The RadButton also provides visual state management and integrates well with command patterns for MVVM design.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadDropDownButton
member.summary:
Represents a customizable drop-down button that combines the functionalities of a standard button and a pop-up. The allows for displaying a drop-down content area when clicked, enabling users to select options or display additional information. This control offers features such as: - Configurable drop-down content and templates - Options to manage the button's open and close behaviors, including automatic closing on Escape or Enter key presses - Control of visibility, position, and dimensions of the drop-down area - Events to handle opening and closing of the drop-down, providing a rich user interaction experience.
The is designed for use in UI scenarios where hierarchical options or extended actions need to be displayed without cluttering the main interface.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadHyperlinkButton
member.summary:
Represents a that functions as a hyperlink button, allowing users to navigate to a specified URI when clicked. The class provides several dependency properties:
: The URI to navigate to upon button click.
: The name of the target window or frame in which the URI should be opened.
: Indicates whether the hyperlink has been clicked at least once.
: Defines the foreground color of the hyperlink after it has been visited.
When the hyperlink button is clicked, it attempts to open the specified URI in the default web browser. The control also supports custom styling and automation peer creation for accessibility.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadSplitButton
member.summary: Represents a split button that facilitates a primary action and offers a drop-down menu with additional supplementary actions. This class includes properties for managing the visibility of its components, the ability to check and uncheck the button, and control over the drop-down menu's appearance and behavior. The RadSplitButton supports events for actions such as clicking the button, opening, closing, and toggling the drop-down. It is designed to be styled and customized, providing features like auto-open delays and command binding for integration into MVVM architectures.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadToggleButton
member.summary: Represents a toggle button control that allows users to switch between two states: checked and unchecked. This control supports customization of corner radius, background visibility, and command binding for a more interactive user experience. The RadToggleButton raises events when activated and allows pre-click handling through the PreviewClick event. It also provides visual state management to reflect different interaction states like mouse over, pressed, and focused.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadToggleSwitchButton
member.summary: Represents a toggle switch button that can display three states: checked, unchecked, and indeterminate. This button extends and provides properties to customize the content and appearance for each state, including options for setting the width and height of the track and thumb, as well as the corner radius of the track in both checked and unchecked states. It also includes animation capabilities for state transitions.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadCallout
member.summary: Represents a customizable callout control that provides various shapes and styles for displaying content in a user-friendly manner. The class allows users to configure properties such as callout type, arrow type, geometry, text alignment, wrapping, trimming, and corner radius, enabling the creation of visually distinct callouts for user interfaces. It inherits from and supports properties for defining geometry and visual appearance, allowing for flexible layouts and detailed customization. Ideal for enhancing user experience with informative overlays that can be styled to match application design.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadCircularProgressBar
member.summary: Represents a circular progress bar that visually indicates progress and completion. The is highly customizable, allowing settings for angles, segments, colors, and more. It inherits from . Key features include: - Customizable start and end angles to define the segment of the circle that represents progress. - Control over the number of segments and their density, enabling varied visual representations. - Support for indeterminate progress state for scenarios where completion cannot be defined. - Options for rounded segments and color ranges for enhanced visual appeal. Usage examples include loading indicators, visual completion meters, or any scenario where a circular representation of progress is required.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.KeyboardModifiers
member.summary: This class presents a way to query the state of the various keyboard modifier keys. It also allows you to check the state of the shortcut key for the current platform.
member.remarks: The different platforms Silverlight runs on employ differing input conventions. Thus shortcuts for common actions such as Copy, Paste and Select All are activated using one key on Windows (Control), but using another on Mac OS X (Apple). Using this class should save you tedious platform checks. It is inadvisable, however, to use the IsShortcutKeyDown property before you've researched what the accepted shortcut for the relevant platform is. Even though this class addresses a Silverlight scenario, it will also work on WPF.

member.remarks: You only need to use this if you wish to mock this class.

member.remarks: You only need to use this if you wish to mock this class.

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.KeyboardModifiers.Modifiers
member.summary: Gets the keyboard modifier keys.

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.KeyboardModifiers.IsShortcutKeyDown
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the platform-specific shortcut meta key is pressed.
member.remarks: For most systems (Windows + Linux) the shortcut key is Control. However, under Mac OS X the shortcut key is Apple (Command). Note that you still have to know if the relevant shortcut on Mac uses Command, because it can be entirely different.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadGlyphExtension
member.summary: Provides a MarkupExtension for rendering glyphs using customizable fonts, sizes, and colors in a WPF application. This class allows the user to set default font properties and provides methods to obtain glyph images or geometries based on specified parameters. It supports dynamic changes to the glyph's size, foreground color, and font name, while ensuring that appropriate validation is in place for input values. The glyph can be rendered as either an image or a path based on the target property type. member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadHighlightTextBlock
member.summary: Represents a customizable text block that highlights specific portions of its text based on predefined criteria. This class extends the control, introducing properties to specify which text to highlight and how to style the highlighted text. It includes features such as case sensitivity, different highlight modes (first match, last match, all matches), and customizable foreground and background colors for the highlighted text. The class supports theming through the interface, allowing it to adapt its style based on the current application theme. The highlighted text is refreshed dynamically when the underlying text or highlight properties change. Additionally, it integrates with the automation framework, enabling accessibility features.

member.name: M:Telerik.Windows.Controls.LayoutDoubleUtil.AreClose(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: AreClose - Returns whether or not two doubles are "close". That is, whether or not they are within epsilon of each other. Note that this epsilon is proportional to the numbers themselves to that AreClose survives scalar multiplication. There are plenty of ways for this to return false even for numbers which are theoretically identical, so no code calling this should fail to work if this returns false. This is important enough to repeat: NB: NO CODE CALLING THIS FUNCTION SHOULD DEPEND ON ACCURATE RESULTS - this should be used for optimizations *only*.
member.returns: Boolean - the result of the AreClose comparison.
member.param: The first double to compare.
The second double to compare.

member.summary: Represents a control that enables navigation within linearly paginated content and can be used as a navigation assistant for other controls, such as the . The provides visual indicators, or "pips," that represent each page, allowing users to easily navigate through them. It supports features such as selectable items, customizable item size and margin, and the ability to specify the maximum number of visible pips. The class also includes automation support to enhance accessibility and provides methods to center the view around the currently selected item.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadTileList
member.summary: Represents a control that displays a collection of tiles in a list format, allowing for easy organization and interaction with the items. The RadTileList supports features like auto-generation of tiles, grouping, and selection handling, as well as layout management for tiles in a customizable manner. It provides various properties to control the appearance and behavior of the tiles, including TileReorderMode for reordering tiles, Grouping capabilities based on a specified property, and support for touch interactions for handling drag-and-drop scenarios.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadExpander
member.summary: Represents a collapsible content control that can expand and collapse to reveal or hide its content. The RadExpander class derives from HeaderedContentControl and implements the IThemable interface. It provides features for handling expansion and collapsing events, customizing the appearance of the header and button, and managing the visual states corresponding to the various expansion directions. The IsExpanded property determines whether the content is currently displayed. The control also includes properties for various header alignments, orientations, and styles, as well as events that notify when the content is expanded or collapsed.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadFluidContentControl
member.summary: The is a specialized content control that dynamically adjusts which of its three content properties is displayed based on the available space. It utilizes customizable thresholds to precisely define the conditions under which the content changes visibility, allowing for seamless transitions between different content states: Small, Normal, and Large. This control is especially useful for responsive designs where the layout adapts to varying screen sizes or layout changes.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadDockPanel
member.summary: Represents a panel that supports docking child elements along the edges (top, bottom, left, right) and allows the last child element to optionally fill the remaining available space. The RadDockPanel facilitates the arrangement of its children based on the specified Dock property, promoting a flexible layout structure suitable for various UI designs. It provides attached properties for setting the Dock position of individual child elements and includes a property to control whether the last child fills the available area. The layout system of RadDockPanel ensures that the child elements are measured and arranged properly during rendering, adapting to changes in size and visibility.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode
member.summary: Describes the placement of where a Popup control appears on the screen.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.Absolute
member.summary: A position of the Popup control relative to the upper-left corner of the screen and at an offset that is defined by the HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset property values. If the screen edge obscures the Popup, the control then repositions itself to align with the edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.Relative
member.summary: A position of the Popup control relative to the upper-left corner of the PlacementTarget and at an offset that is defined by the HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset property values. If the screen edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself to align with the screen edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.Bottom
member.summary: A position of the Popup control where the control aligns its upper edge with the lower edge of the PlacementTarget and aligns its left edge with the left edge of the PlacementTarget. If the lower screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself so that its lower edge aligns with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget. If the upper screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control then repositions itself so that its upper edge aligns with the upper screen-edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.Center
member.summary: A position of the Popup control where it is centered over the PlacementTarget. If a screen edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself to align with the screen edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.Right
member.summary: A position of the Popup control that aligns its left edge with the right edge of the PlacementTarget and aligns its upper edge with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget. If the right screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself so that its left edge aligns with the left edge of the PlacementTarget. If the left screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself so that its left edge aligns with the left screen-edge. If the upper or lower screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control then repositions itself to align with the obscuring screen edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.AbsolutePoint
member.summary: A position of the Popup control relative to the upper-left corner of the screen and at an offset that is defined by the HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset property values. If the screen edge obscures the Popup, the control extends in the opposite direction from the axis defined by the HorizontalOffset or VerticalOffset.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.RelativePoint
member.summary: A position of the Popup control relative to the upper-left corner of the PlacementTarget and at an offset that is defined by the HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset property values. If a screen edge obscures the Popup, the Popup extends in the opposite direction from the direction from the axis defined by the HorizontalOffset or VerticalOffset. If the opposite screen edge also obscures the Popup, the control then aligns with this screen edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.Mouse
member.summary: A position of the Popup control that aligns its upper edge with the lower edge of the bounding box of the mouse and aligns its left edge with the left edge of the bounding box of the mouse. If the lower screen-edge obscures the Popup, it repositions itself to align with the upper edge of the bounding box of the mouse. If the upper screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself to align with the upper screen-edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.MousePoint
member.summary: A position of the Popup control relative to the tip of the mouse cursor and at an offset that is defined by the HorizontalOffset and VerticalOffset property values. If a horizontal or vertical screen edge obscures the Popup, it opens in the opposite direction from the obscuring edge. If the opposite screen edge also obscures the Popup, it then aligns with the obscuring screen edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.Left
member.summary: A Popup control that aligns its right edge with the left edge of the PlacementTarget and aligns its upper edge with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget. If the left screen-edge obscures the Popup, the Popup repositions itself so that its left edge aligns with the right edge of the PlacementTarget. If the right screen-edge obscures the Popup, the right edge of the control aligns with the right screen-edge. If the upper or lower screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself to align with the obscuring screen edge.

member.name: F:Telerik.Windows.Controls.PlacementMode.Top
member.summary: A position of the Popup control that aligns its lower edge with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget and aligns its left edge with the left edge of the PlacementTarget. If the upper screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself so that its upper edge aligns with the lower edge of the PlacementTarget. If the lower screen-edge obscures the Popup, the lower edge of the control aligns with the lower screen-edge. If the left or right screen-edge obscures the Popup, it then repositions itself to align with the obscuring screen.

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.DoubleRangeBase.IsSelectionRangeEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether the RadSlider can displays a selection range. This is a dependency property.
member.remarks: The SelectionStart and SelectionEnd properties define a selection range and must be set for the selection range to appear when IsSelectionRangeEnabled is set to true.

example.code: <telerik:RadSlider x:Name="radSlider1" Width="100" IsSelectionRangeEnabled="True" />

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.DoubleRangeBase.IsCoercionSuppressed
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether the slider should coerce the setting of related properties like Value, SelectionStart, SelectionEnd, Minimum, Maximum, MinimumRangeSpan and MaximumRangeSpan.
member.remarks: If set to True, the coercion is done only when the user manipulates the slider and not if the related properties are set by code or through binding.

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.DoubleRangeBase.SelectionRange
member.summary: Gets the difference between SelectionStart and SelectionEnd.
member.value: The difference between SelectionStart and SelectionEnd.

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.DoubleRangeBase.Selection
member.summary: Gets or sets the selection - SelectionStart and SelectionEnd.
member.value: The selection.

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.DoubleRangeBase.SelectionEnd
member.summary: Gets or sets the largest value of a specified selection.
member.remarks: The value of the SelectionEnd property cannot be greater than the value of the Maximum property and cannot be less than the value of the Minimum property. The value of the SelectionEnd property must also be greater than or equal to the value of the SelectionStart property. If the value of the SelectionEnd property is greater than the value of the Maximum property or less than the value of the Minimum property, the value is set to the value of the Maximum or Minimum property respectively.

example.code: <telerik:RadSlider x:Name="radSlider1" Width="100" Orientation="Horizontal" Minimum="0" Maximum="10" TickPlacement="TopLeft" TickFrequency="1" IsSelectionRangeEnabled="True" SelectionEnd="8" SelectionStart="6"/>

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.DoubleRangeBase.SelectionStart
member.summary: Gets or sets the smallest value of a specified selection.
member.remarks: IsSelectionRangeEnabled must be True in order to use SelectionStart and SelectionEnd The value of the SelectionStart property cannot be less than the value of the Minimum property and cannot be greater than the value of the Maximum property. The value of the SelectionEnd property must also be greater than or equal to the value of the SelectionStart property. If SelectionStart is less than Minimum or greater than Maximum, SelectionStart is set to the value of Minimum or Maximum respectively.

example.code: <telerik:RadSlider x:Name="radSlider1" Width="100" Orientation="Horizontal" Minimum="0" Maximum="10" TickPlacement="TopLeft" TickFrequency="1" IsSelectionRangeEnabled="True" SelectionEnd="8" SelectionStart="6"/>

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.DoubleRangeBase.MinimumRangeSpan
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum value distance between SelectionStart and SelectionEnd.
member.remarks: The IsSelectionRangeEnabled property of RadSlider has to be set to True.

example.code: <telerik:RadSlider x:Name="radSlider1" Width="100" IsSelectionRangeEnabled="True" MinimumRangeSpan="0.1"/>

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.DoubleRangeBase.MaximumRangeSpan
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum value distance between SelectionStart and SelectionEnd.
member.remarks: The IsSelectionRangeEnabled property of RadSlider has to be set to True.

example.code: <telerik:RadSlider x:Name="radSlider1" Width="100" IsSelectionRangeEnabled="True" MaximumRangeSpan="0.1"/>

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadSlider
member.summary: Represents a slider control that allows users to select a value from a specified range. The enables users to make precise selections by sliding a thumb along a track, with support for both single and multiple range selections. It offers various customization options for appearance and behavior, such as styling the thumbs, setting tooltips for enhanced usability, and enabling snapping to tick marks. This control provides user-friendly interaction for modifying values seamlessly within a designated range, making it suitable for applications requiring value selection with visual feedback.

Slider control lets the user select from a range of values by moving a slider. Slider is used to enable to user to gradually modify a value (range selection). Slider is an easy and natural interface for users, because it provides good visual feedback.

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadSlider.IsDirectionReversed
member.summary: Gets or sets the direction of increasing value. This is a dependency property.
member.remarks:
The value of this property determines the direction of increasing value of a RadRadSlider.
For example, when you move the thumb control up on a vertical RadSlider when the IsDirectionReversed property is set to false, the Value of the RadSlider increases. If the value of the IsDirectionReversed property is changed to true, the Value of the RadSlider decreases as the thumb moves up.

member.name: P:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadSlider.IsMoveToPointEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether the thumb of a RadSlider moves immediately to the location of the mouse click that occurs while the mouse pointer pauses on the RadSlider track. This is a dependency property.
member.remarks: When this property is set to false and a mouse click occurs along the RadSlider away from the thumb, the thumb moves in the direction of the mouse click. Instead of moving immediately to the mouse click location, the thumb moves a distance that is defined by the RepeatInterval property for each mouse click. The effect of multiple mouse clicks can be emulated by pressing and holding the left mouse button until the thumb is repositioned to the desired location.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadSlideView
member.summary: Represents a navigation control that allows users to slide between different views, enabling swipe gestures to navigate through a collection of items. This class provides functionality to configure the presentation and transition animations of the items and manage the visibility of navigation buttons. It supports both horizontal and vertical orientation for item display and allows customization of swipe behavior, including the handling of swiping thresholds to determine when the displayed view should change. This control is suitable for implementing galleries, item carousels, or any scenario where a smooth transition between views is desired.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadSvgImage
member.summary: Represents a control for displaying SVG images in a WPF application. The class allows for the rendering of SVG files or XML strings as visual content, providing various properties for customization such as , , , and options to override colors and stroke widths. It supports animations and custom brushes, enabling the user to tailor the SVG image's appearance to fit specific requirements. The class integrates with the WPF rendering system, ensuring appropriate measurement and layout through dependency properties such as . Additionally, it handles loading SVG data from various sources, including local files and URI schemes, while maintaining the application’s context through the property.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadTaskBoard
member.summary: Represents a task board control that allows users to display and manage tasks in a visual manner. The provides features for organizing tasks into columns, enabling drag-and-drop functionality, and responding to user interactions through touch and click events. Users can customize columns, control their widths, heights, and templates, and manage task grouping through various properties and events. The control supports automatic generation of columns based on the provided data source and allows for the addition, removal, and reordering of tasks with smooth animation and visual feedback.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadTaskBoardCard
member.summary: Represents a card in a task board, allowing the display and manipulation of task-related information such as assignees, tags, icons, and categories. The class inherits from and provides various dependency properties to define its visual elements, including the task ID, assignee, associated tags, and templates for displaying icons and tags. It also offers functionality for resolving the category brush based on the specified category name and provides options to show or hide category indicators. The card is designed to be used within a and supports customization through styles and templates.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadToolTip
member.summary: Represents a customizable tooltip control that can be attached to other UI elements. The class inherits from and provides properties to control the tooltip's appearance and behavior, including its offset, visibility, placement, and the target element it is associated with. The tooltip can dynamically open and close, allowing for interactive user experiences.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadToolTipService
member.summary: The class provides a comprehensive service for managing tooltips in a WPF application. It enables the user to customize tooltip behavior through various properties and events, such as show and hide delays, position offsets, and tooltip content. This service supports the attachment of events for tooltip opening and closing, and facilitates dynamic updates to tooltips as the user interacts with UI elements. Furthermore, it manages the display of tooltips based on user actions (like mouse movement) and conditions, allowing for an enhanced user experience through rich tooltip customization.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadTransitionControl
member.summary: Represents a control that provides transition animations for its content using different transition effects and easing functions. The RadTransitionControl inherits from ContentControl and allows customization of the transition's duration, easing function, and transition effect. It includes properties to determine if the transition is idle, as well as events to handle transition status changes and triggering. This control leverages templates for its presentation and can be styled as needed.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadPasswordBox
member.summary: Represents a password input control that allows users to enter passwords securely. This control masks the input with a specified character (default is a bullet character '●'), and provides options to show the password through a button that toggles visibility. It also supports password-related events, including notifying when the password changes. The secure password is stored using to protect sensitive data against memory inspection. Additional features include customizable button content, and visibility controls for the password display button.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.Controls.RadWatermarkTextBox
member.summary: Represents a customizable TextBox control that displays watermark text and allows for additional label functionality. The includes properties for defining and styling a label, managing the visibility of watermark content based on the focused state, and provides dependency properties for maintaining text, selection behavior, and additional content. It features animations for label transitions and supports themes for visual customization. This control is designed to enhance user experience by providing contextual information and interaction cues when input fields are empty or untitled.

member.summary:
Represents the automation peer for the control, providing support for UI automation and control patterns. This class enables interaction with the RadBusyIndicator from automated UI test frameworks and exposes the properties and behaviors of the RadBusyIndicator control for accessibility.
It implements the and interfaces, allowing automated tools to read and manipulate the control's busy state and value through the UI Automation framework. The automation peer also offers additional metadata such as localized control type, control name, and control status.

member.summary: Represents the automation peer for a RadExpander control, enabling UI automation support for the control's expand and collapse functionality. This class inherits from FrameworkElementAutomationPeer and implements the IExpandCollapseProvider interface. It provides functionality to determine the expanded or collapsed state of the control, as well as methods to expand and collapse the content. The class also supports retrieving the associated control patterns, automation control type, and details about the control such as its name and properties. It ensures that operations can only be performed on an enabled instance of RadExpander and raises appropriate automation events when the expand/collapse state changes.

member.name: T:Telerik.Windows.InheritanceContextPropagator
member.summary: This class is used to propagate inheritance context to non-visual class instances that might be part of the WPF control element tree. Note that while it relies on the special notion that Freezable classes have for "inheritance context", you should not rely on any other characteristics that Freezable objects usually have (cloning, freezing, etc.). Actually this object will explicitly prevent the framework from freezing its instances and it will generally behave as any other non-Freezable object.

member.summary: Represents event data for routed events in the Rad framework, inheriting from the RoutedEventArgs class. This class provides information about the routed event, such as the event identifier, the source of the event, and its handling status. member.name: M:Telerik.Windows.DragDrop.DragDropManager.AddDragInitializeHandler(System.Windows.DependencyObject,Telerik.Windows.DragDrop.DragInitializeEventHandler,System.Boolean)
